Edward Snowden has been hailed by some as a whistleblower and hero. He claims to have carefully selected a few classified documents to protect the American people from civil liberties abuses. But the numbers and timeline tell a different story.

First, a little reflection shows the sheer size of the heist is too large to be handled by the known resources.

  • Number of documents Snowden stole = 1.2 M.
  • Time to skim each document = 30 seconds.
  • Total time to skim all documents = 600,000 minutes = 1,250 man-days.
  • Time available to review documents = March through May 2013 = 90 calendar days.
  • Minimum number of personnel to skim documents = 1250 / 90 = 14.

Therefore Snowden could never have reviewed the documents in the time available. He claims he is a loyal patriot, who carefully sorted out a few documents about abuses of civil liberties. He claims he held back legitimate national security secrets to protect the country he loves. In reality, he defected while in possession of a vast trove of unsorted, unreviewed documents. Many of those documents probably contained critical national security secrets that a true patriot would never have disclosed. Therefore he is a liar and traitor.

To put it in more everyday terms, if printed out the documents would have weighed 50,000 pounds and filled a semi trailer. We are seriously expected to believe one lone patriot could have made a dent in that in the three months he had available? While stealing the documents and planning a defection? That's a whopper of a non-conspiracy theory.

Moreover, the documents published all made the U.S. look bad. There was not a single document about, say, a dumbass forklift operator driving a prong through a pallet of computers. There was not one single pedestrian, everyday document that could have been used to prove the accuracy of the documents without disclosing classified information. No, the release was carefully crafted to score political points. It's simply impossible for an IT specialist to grab a bunch of random documents and come up with only damning revelations.

Connect the dots:

  • Dozens of people reviewed the documents for months.
  • Those people were foreigners.
  • They released only documents humiliating the U.S. government and allies.
  • The documents were released in staged media circuses.

The natural conclusion is that the so-called "Snowden" information releases were carefully stage-managed by a foreign intelligence service. The lopsided content of the releases was intended to serve as a smokescreen.
